title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): P is a combinatorial n-gon with vertex set S and edge set A, drawn on the equator of the Riemann sphere Σ. The vertices are punctures R_s, each edge a has a midpoint Q_a, and the two poles P_ω and P_ω' are the centres of the two faces. The base point is P_ω. D_P is the dihedral group of order 2n; ω is the rotation fixing the orientation; τ is complex conjugation, the reflection in the equator. Grothendieck is computing a diamond of fundamental groups (54): Π, Π^D, Π^τ (Π^Σ on the previous page) and Π^{D,τ}. These are orbifold fundamental groups of Σ_P^* = Σ minus the n vertices, and of its quotients by D_P, by {1,τ} and by both. The aim is explicit presentations with distinguished generators. This page does three things.
(1) Π_P. The loops ρ_s = λ_a λ_{ω'(a)}^{-1} encircle the vertex s, and (59) gives ρ_{n-1}…ρ_0 = 1. (60) states Π_P ≅ ⟨ρ_0,…,ρ_{n-1} | ρ_{n-1}…ρ_0 = 1⟩, the standard presentation of the free group of rank n-1 = π_1(P^1 minus n points). It is rigidified by choosing a 'repère' (s_0, a(s_0,ω)), i.e. an isomorphism with the standard polygon P_0.
(2) Π^τ. This is the orbifold π_1 of Σ_P^*/τ: a closed hemisphere whose boundary is cut into n mirror arcs by the n punctures. The generators are τ_a = (λ_a, τ), a path from P_ω to τ(P_ω) = P_ω' followed by τ. This makes τ_a the reflection in the mirror arc a, so τ_a^2 = 1. (62) gives Π^τ = *_{a∈A} Z/2, the free product of n copies of Z/2, i.e. the reflection group of an ideal hyperbolic n-gon. Π_P is its index-2 'even' subgroup. (63) gives ρ_s = τ_a τ_{a'}, where a, a' are the two edges at s and a = ω(a'). With τ_i = τ_{ω^i a_0} one gets ρ_i = τ_i τ_{i-1}. The relation (59) then telescopes from τ_i^2 = 1, and (62 bis) is the presentation ⟨τ_0,…,τ_{n-1} | τ_i^2 = 1⟩.
(3) Toward Π^{D,τ}. Orientation-preserving elements of D_P (rotations) fix the pole P_ω, while reflections exchange the poles. The stabiliser of P_ω in D_P × {1,τ} is therefore {(g, τ^{α(g)})}, with α(g) = 0 or 1 according as sg(g) = ±1. This is a copy of D_P, which the next page uses to split Π^{D,τ} → D_P and to define ρ = ω̃, σ̃_a, σ_a, ε_s. Overall this is the explicit combinatorial bookkeeping of the 'cyclotomic map' (the polygon dessin) and its real/dihedral orbifold quotients, in service of the Teichmüller tower for genus 0. It also touches the real moduli M_{0,n}(R), whose cells are indexed by dihedral orderings.
errors: No mathematical errors. The telescoping check holds: ρ_{n-1}…ρ_0 = τ_{n-1}(τ_{n-2}τ_{n-2})…(τ_0τ_0)τ_{-1} = τ_{n-1}^2 = 1, using τ_{-1} = τ_{n-1}.
The rank count is consistent: the index-2 even subgroup of (Z/2)^{*n} is free of rank n-1, matching (60).
The marginal note warns about an index/notation convention (τ_i versus τ_{a_0}, relative to the choice of a_0). It is a bookkeeping caveat, not a mathematical error.
The stabiliser description is correct: rotations fix P_ω, and reflections swap P_ω and P_ω', which is compensated by τ.

ideas.what: Presentation of π_1 of the sphere minus the n vertices of an equatorial polygon by vertex loops with product 1, rigidified by a choice of repère (flag).
ideas.modern_name: Standard presentation of π_1(P^1 − {n points}); base point/tangential data given by the dessin
ideas.where_published: Generally in the spirit of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), cyclotomic maps/dessins

ideas.what: The orbifold fundamental group of the quotient by complex conjugation is a free product of n copies of Z/2, generated by the reflections in the edges; the vertex loops are products of adjacent reflections.
ideas.modern_name: Reflection (Coxeter) group of an ideal hyperbolic polygon; real-structure orbifold π_1; the 'real' fundamental group of P^1 minus real points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré polygon theorem, Coxeter); in an arithmetic context, later work on real points and complex conjugation in Galois–Teichmüller theory

ideas.what: Section of D_P into D_P × {1,τ} as the stabiliser of the pole, twisting reflections by τ according to orientation sign. This splits π^{D,τ} → D_P and leads to the generators ρ, σ_a, ε_s.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the orbifold fundamental group extension 1 → Π → Π^{D,τ} → D × Z/2 via a fixed point (base point at a fixed pole)

missed.claim: This is a systematic, base-point-careful computation of the full diamond of orbifold fundamental groups (Π, Π^D, Π^τ, Π^{D,τ}) for the regular polygon dessin with its real structure. It is an unpublished precursor of explicit treatments of complex conjugation and dihedral symmetry in genus-0 Galois–Teichmüller theory. The content itself is classical.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that by 1981 Grothendieck was working out real/dihedral orbifold structures of M_{0,n}-type objects with explicit generators. Nothing on this page appears mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but classical computations: free group presentations, the reflection group of an ideal polygon, and a stabiliser splitting. They are of historical interest as part of the Teichmüller-tower program, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '(du reste que les relations (59) est conséquence…' should read '(de sorte que la relation (59) est conséquence des relations τ_i^2 = 1)'.
'donc (s_0,a_0) repère conduisant' probably reads 'donc (s_0,a_0) repère ω-direct', followed by 'on pose … par (64)'.

Marginal note (left, rotated) is only partly legible. It appears to warn that the τ_0 (and τ_i) notation here should not be confused with τ_{a_0}, because of how a_0 is chosen; the exact wording is uncertain.
In (63) the struck-out words precede 'avec a = a(s,ω)'; the reading 'i.e. a = ω(a') i.e. a' = ω'(a)' is correct.
'Venons-en à Π^τ' is correct, and (61) is τ_a = (λ_a, τ) ∈ Π_P^τ (a ∈ A).
In (66) the condition is sg(g) = 1 or -1 (the sign/orientation character of g), as transcribed.
